$comment: L2D-05-KEY-FORMAT: keyboard shortcut contracts for character/paragraph formatting (ledger kind=shortcut, feature ids shortcut.*). Every entry is a key-trigger chord (no selector); the runner's placeCaret selects the first word (Chromium focuses the contenteditable on selection placement, so the #editor keydown handler receives the chord). All chords verified in the C1 SHORTCUT PARITY block of editor.js (editor.addEventListener("keydown"), ~line 10965). Assertions mirror the proven click contracts in home-format.json (same emitCommand targets).

shortcut.bold.note: ledger row: shortcut.bold (Ctrl+B) — emitCommand("bold"), same execCommand path as the proven toolbar click contract 'bold'; <b> wrap -> font-weight 700

shortcut.italic.note: ledger row: shortcut.italic (Ctrl+I) — emitCommand("italic"); <i> wrap -> font-style italic

shortcut.underline.note: ledger row: shortcut.underline (Ctrl+U) — emitCommand("underline"); <u> wrap (reached by the runner's closest b,i,u,span,p reader)

shortcut.strikeout.note: ledger row: shortcut.strikeout (Ctrl+Shift+X PC variant; OO Shift+Cmd+X Mac) — emitCommand("strikeThrough"); <strike> wrap read via the reader's || el fallback

shortcut.subscript.note: ledger row: shortcut.subscript (Ctrl+.) — emitCommand("subscript"); <sub> wrap -> vertical-align sub (same as the proven subscript click contract)

shortcut.superscript.note: ledger row: shortcut.superscript (Ctrl+,) — emitCommand("superscript"); <sup> wrap -> vertical-align super

shortcut.centerpara.note: ledger row: shortcut.centerpara (Ctrl+E) — emitCommand("justifyCenter"), same command as the proven justifycenter click contract

shortcut.rightpara.note: ledger row: shortcut.rightpara (Ctrl+R; the keydown preventDefault also suppresses browser reload while focused) — emitCommand("justifyRight")

shortcut.leftpara.note: ledger row: shortcut.leftpara — ledger + editor.js bind Ctrl+L (Ctrl+Shift+L is the bulleted-list combo, insertUnorderedList). On the default left-aligned document justifyLeft is a parity no-op: Chromium skips the style write, so the honest post-chord state is start (same as the justifyleft click contract)

shortcut.indent.note: ledger row: shortcut.indent (Ctrl+M) — execCommand("indent"); Chromium wraps the block in <blockquote style="margin: 0 0 0 40px"> — the wrapper's existence is the observable effect (the inner block's own margin-left stays 0px)

shortcut.increasefontsize.note: ledger row: shortcut.increasefontsize (Ctrl+]) — emitCommand("fontSizeInc") steps the CSS absolute size; probed: default 32px h1 word wrapped in <span style="font-size: xxx-large"> -> computed 48px

shortcut.decreasefontsize.note: ledger row: shortcut.decreasefontsize (Ctrl+[) — emitCommand("fontSizeDec"); probed: default 32px h1 word wrapped in <span style="font-size: x-large"> -> computed 24px

shortcut.smallcaps.note: ledger row: shortcut.smallcaps (Ctrl+Shift+K) — emitCommand("smallCaps") -> toggleInlineCSS("fontVariant","small-caps"), which wraps via execCommand("insertHTML") and leaves the caret collapsed — a computed-style read on the selection can never pass, so the contract asserts the wrap span itself (probed: <span style="font-variant-caps: small-caps"> -> computed font-variant small-caps)

$skipped.reason: Ctrl+Shift+M is bound (emitCommand("outdent"), native execCommand) but the contract layer has no pre vocabulary that builds indented paragraph state first (file-menu/list/ctx-menu/backstage only), and probed execCommand("outdent") on the runner's unindented fixture is a structural no-op — no post-chord assertion can distinguish the chord firing from not firing, so any assertion would pass vacuously
